title: the live census tooth names the conjunct that failed and its entries
intention: The outside-readers census proof's live tooth, when it reds, names the conjunct that failed and the entries that failed it, so a red is a finding rather than a coin toss.
why: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces, permanent in records of truth) and Law 3: the 6437cfd935bb build commit f8a4ab57f resealed cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_a_census_names_every_outside_reader.py RED on tooth 4 (the_live_census_completes_over_every_root), rc=1, killed=[], no timeout; its FAIL detail is cut at 300 chars by check() and ends mid-root ('/home/akien/dev/src/CC0AC-W'), every root visible reading 'scanned', so which of its four conjuncts failed (declared root set, status, stray inside path, row shape) is in no record (/home/akien/.cairn/logs/tester/0/runs/test-f2ad7cda1556); by hand 30 min later every conjunct held.
how: Lift tooth 4's predicate into a function over a census result that returns the failed conjuncts with their entries; tooth 4 prints them whole on FAIL. A new proof cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_the_live_census_tooth_names_what_failed.py drives that function over a scratch census (O.census over scratch roots, one declared root dropped from its roots).

clauses.claim: when tooth 4's predicate fails, its FAIL line names each conjunct that failed (declared root set, root status, stray inside path, row shape) and the offending entries in full, never a detail cut short
